The roof

Single panel

Components

The battery is LG Chem, lithium batteries with guaranteed minimum life of 10 years. The controller has a cell antenna so I can not only monitor performance from my phone, I can have support go in and configure and fix it for me. Since I know a bit about hardware, it is trivial for me to go in and disconnect or even completely remove the cell antenna. Should shit happen, that's the first thing I'm going to do. No one needs to know if my system is working except me.

Now for the particulars but without system specifics (which if you need, I can dredge up from the paperwork).

About the only things not hooked into the solar are the AC, stove, microwave, dryer, garage, one room and one outlet in another (total of three outlets not covered not counting garage). My normal power usage gives me about 5 days on the battery. I can, however, run literally everything connected except for one of the three following: griddle, toaster, toaster oven... if I turn on everything including those three, it pulls too much and the controller shuts down the power. Leave off one of those three and it's fine).

Total cost of the system was $32,000 but that's pretty much permanent support including work by them to remove and reinstall the equipment (at no charge) when I have to have my roof (eventually) replaced.

Because I'm on net metering, the power company pays me for the power I pump out at the same rate that they would charge me for the same amount of power. And since I'm generating quite a bit for a home, I won't be using much power off of the grid on any normal day which means it always generates a check from the power company.

  1. If you are the type to do financing, you can do it no money down. Since this happened in less than a year of my house purchase, I mentally consider this part of the house and mortgage payment (even though it's to a different company and everything counts it as not part of the house except taxes .... so my tax value should go up the value of the solar setup). This system is $32,000 (there's a lot to that, though so don't let it knock you out of your chair). The monthly payment is $175 (10 years) but there are strings to that too. TL;DR: No money down, doable if you can handle monthly payments but the financial math will never work out until you pay it off.

  2. The "one" battery is the new lithium batteries - I know, lithium... this has a manufacturer's warranty of 10 years and that's even if you cycle it every day. It's a single unit because it's small enough to be a single unit :) The enclosure is outdoor safe as it the meter, inverter, control box. This is actually a HUGE battery, if it were the older style, it would be a bank of batteries on the floor. I include heat on mine but not AC, dryer, stove. Washer is on it simply because it's on the same circuit as the deep freeze.

So the major "must have" components there were on the list to power in an outage were: Fridge, Freezer, Heater (gas heat, hypothermia sucks), a few lights, a few outlets for things like computer or TV since those components use so little power.

Now all that said, my normal power usage means I could go 5 days without any sunlight at all.

The part that annoys me is that the financing company I had to go through (long story) required that the battery capacity match the solar output. <sigh> That means more battery than I really need. But, on the other hand, I can have pretty much every light on, washer, freezer, fridge, heater, and 2 counter-top appliances (but not 3).

The cost includes pretty much permanent support from the installing company. If I have issues, they will drive out and fix it. If I have to replace my roof, they will take the equipment down and reinstall it, even provide me with a roofing company if I want. They support every part of this system from top to bottom, from purchase through the expected lifetime of the system (which is 20+ years).
